answer: In sponsor-convex admission, a relic is a fresh clone trying to enter; it must anchor in the shared atlas, where duplicate sponsor keys, clusters and hardware collide. Each relic needs three unrelated sponsors from separate branches to burn onyx equal to the square of identities they have backed this epoch, so 1,000 heads need disjoint sponsors and a rising bill in onyx, not parallel fees. It fails if sponsors collude, onyx is lent, or branch proofs in the atlas are forgeable.
